body: Congrats {player_name}! You have been picked for the Northstar Wellness Draw. Reply YES to meet your prize concierge.[[t4]][[t5]]

tells.flag: You did not enter any draw, and no such programme was announced on the intranet

explanation: A small 'win' gets you to reply, which confirms your number is active and starts a conversation.

subject: Your employer bonus pool
body: Your employer has enrolled you in a loyalty bonus pool worth up to $450. To begin, please confirm your staff ID and date of birth.[[t3]][[t5]]

tells.flag: An unfamiliar outside company claims to speak for your employer and asks for personal data

tells.text: Bonuses unclaimed after 24 hours return to the pool.

tells.flag: Asks for a photo of your badge
tells.text: Send a photo of your staff badge to speed things up.

explanation: A reward story justifies collecting personal details that can be used in later, more convincing attacks.

body: Finish our 2-minute culture survey and get a $50 e-voucher. Sign in with your work password at culture-survey.example/start to begin.[[t4]][[t5]]

tells.flag: A survey should never ask for your work password

tells.text: Your vouchar will be emailed instantly.

explanation: The prize is bait; the password prompt is the real goal. Legitimate surveys use your normal single sign-on, not a typed-in password on a new site.

subject: Reminder: unclaimed $450
body: Your $450 bonus is still unclaimed. To release it we just need a small $12 processing fee, paid by voucher code.[[t3]][[t5]]

tells.flag: Real rewards never require you to pay a fee first

tells.text: Many of your colleagues have already claimed theirs.
Reply with the voucher code and a photo of the receipt.

explanation: Advance-fee scam. Once you have invested a little (data, a reply), a small payment seems reasonable.
